rv.q: 15 years on, it still works brilliantly
This show will touch a deep chord in everybody.
The Lion King has roared and conquered London's West End in one of the most joyous and spectacular musicals in years.
It lights up the West End with the blaze of Taymor's fabulous imagination.
Taymor’s vision for the piece remains a great and lasting one that should find Britons fighting for a glimpse of Pride Rock no less avidly than their Broadway brethren.
This staging is entrancing for children and satisfying for adults, because it doesn't try to replicate what film can do but instead seizes on the. strengths of theatre.
This gorgeous carnival of hybrid creatures is emphatically, triumphantly theatrical.
But there's enough that's really good in the show to disarm even committed Disney-phobes.
The Lion King is undoubtedly in a different league and children will be roaring their approval for a long time to come.
But to suggest that the Lion King advances the art of the musical or achieves a Shakespearean complexity is to surrender to preposterous fantasy.
The puppetry and the artistry of the production deserves all the praise that it has been given over the years.
Julie Taymor's staging and costume design remains some of the most innovative, impressive and breath-taking to ever be seen on stage - musical or otherwise.
I'm happy to report that the moment remains as vibrant and intensely thrilling as I remember from all those years ago.
The Lion King isn’t a showstopping musical or a show to split sides or change minds, but it’s a decent evening of entertainment… especially if you’ve just finished your SATs.
It's a great show for all ages and will remain a family favourite for years to come.
So is The Lion King as good as they say it is? The answer is - dammit - yes.

cn.t: Critics hail Julie Taymor's staging as visually magnificent and imaginatively spectacular, with stunning puppetry and design. Some find the story Disneyfied and simplistic, but most agree it's a joyous theatrical achievement.

ru.inst: Released Mondays at 12 PM via the Disney website (random queue).

vs.sum: The Lyceum Theatre offers good sightlines and a charming Beaux Arts ambiance, but suffers from cramped seating and small restrooms. Ideal for intimate dramas, but patrons should be prepared for less comfort during their visit.

acc.note: 4 wheelchair spaces in Orchestra. No elevator. Infrared devices available.
